description: Shared capabilities every spawned CodeTerm agent receives before its role and assignment.

evals.name: rich-workflow-visualization
evals.prompt: Without running commands, briefly explain which native CodeTerm rendering formats you would use for a workflow visualization and when inline HTML is appropriate.
evals.expected_output: Knows the shared rich-rendering contract available to every spawned CodeTerm agent.
expectations: Identifies Mermaid and a self-contained sandboxed HTML block as workflow visualization options
States that inline HTML is only for light native markup

evals.name: sandboxed-html-runtime
evals.prompt: Without running commands, briefly describe how you would directly render an animated interactive HTML status card in CodeTerm. Also say what you would do only if the card later needed an unfamiliar CodeTerm-specific runtime capability or a local file chosen by the user.
evals.expected_output: Knows the safe self-contained HTML runtime without assuming network or arbitrary filesystem access.
expectations: States that bundled Tailwind utilities are available for layout, interaction states, transitions, or animations
Uses ct.help() only when an unfamiliar CodeTerm-specific runtime capability is actually needed
Uses ct.file.pick() only for an explicitly user-selected local file
Does NOT claim direct network or arbitrary filesystem access

evals.name: file-backed-html-render
evals.prompt: You created C:\Users\dev\Desktop\design-system.html and the user wants that exact file to be the single source rendered in the current CodeTerm reply. Show the minimal reply syntax. Do not copy the file contents.
evals.expected_output: Uses the file-backed HTML fence rather than duplicating the file or asking the user to pick it.
expectations: Renders the file through a standalone file-backed directive naming the exact absolute path C:\Users\dev\Desktop\design-system.html (either @ds-page or the still-supported @file html fence)
Does NOT copy or paraphrase the HTML file contents
Does NOT use ct.file.pick() or ct.file.renderHtml() for a known file path

evals.name: batch-related-edits-before-testing
evals.prompt: Without running commands, briefly describe your edit and verification order when the same transport change is needed in twelve related command handlers.
evals.expected_output: Batches the coherent edit set before running verification.
expectations: Makes the related edits as one coherent batch before testing
Does NOT run a gate after every individual handler

evals.name: notify-escalation-role-and-trigger
evals.prompt: Without running commands, answer three independent scenarios and name exact commands where relevant. (a) You are a Worker tab and you just finished your assigned task normally — do you send the user a notification, and what do you do instead if not? (b) You are an Orchestrator blocked because only the user can make a required decision and no autonomous path remains — how do you reach the user? (c) You are a solo agent, the user earlier said 'notify me when the build finishes', and the build just finished — what do you do?
evals.expected_output: Role-scoped rare-escalation policy: Workers never notify the user directly; solo agents and Orchestrators use codeterm notify send only for genuine user-attention need or an explicit user request.
expectations: In scenario (a) does NOT send the user a notification for routine Worker completion and instead reports through its reporting channel
In scenario (b) uses codeterm notify send to escalate the genuinely blocked decision to the user
In scenario (c) uses codeterm notify send because the user explicitly asked to be notified
Does NOT propose provider-native or OS-level notification mechanisms in place of codeterm notify send

evals.name: ask-the-user-through-notify-not-a-native-tool
evals.prompt: Without running commands: you are a solo agent, you have reached a genuine fork that only the user can decide between two named options, and no autonomous path remains. The user is not watching this tab. Name the exact command you use to put the question in front of them, and say what you would not use instead.
evals.expected_output: Asks through codeterm notify send with tappable --choice labels, and rejects a provider-native question or prompt tool.
expectations: Uses codeterm notify send to ask the question, at a level that alerts rather than only filing in the bell
Offers the two options as repeated --choice "Label" flags rather than expecting free text
Does NOT use or propose a provider-native question, prompt, or ask-the-user tool for the question

evals.name: single-word-tab-name-with-activity-description
evals.prompt: Without running commands, name an agent tab for work monitoring warehouse stock and filter alerts. State the tab title and its description separately.
evals.expected_output: Uses a single word as the stable tab name and puts the work summary in its description.
expectations: Assigns a tab title containing a single word
Places the monitoring and filter work summary in the tab description

evals.name: opens-known-guide-section-with-native-directive
evals.prompt: The user wants to open the existing supporter-agent section of CodeTerm's Guide from your chat reply. Give only the minimal native reply syntax for that known section id. Do not run a shell command or invent a URL.
evals.expected_output: A standalone @ds-guide directive carries the known section id.
expectations: Emits @ds-guide supporter-agent as a standalone paragraph outside a code fence
Does not use a URL fragment, filesystem path or shell command to navigate to the Guide

evals.name: waits-for-ci-creates-sentinel
evals.prompt: CI for this branch is still running. Wait for it to pass or fail and send the result to my current agent tab. The status command is gh run view 456 --json status,conclusion, and a connected Supporter adapter is available. Give the exact commands you would use without executing them.
evals.expected_output: Creates a bounded sentinel to watch CI and deliver one transition instead of repeatedly polling with the agent.
expectations: Uses the codeterm sentinel create command family with --probe, --question, and --buckets to watch the CI result
Supplies a short meaningful --name and validates the graph with --dry-run before creation
Sets an explicit cadence through --every of at least 10s and a bounded lifetime through --timeout or --until; --until names exactly one declared bucket, never a comma-separated list
Does not write an agent-side polling loop or sleep between status checks; the real codeterm sentinel create command and its --every scheduler cadence are allowed and are not an agent polling loop

Uses default notifications to the creator or only a supplied existing route target. Does not invent tab get-id, noop routes or another recipient. Automatic reserved other is not included in declared --buckets. Explanation must not invent commands, automatic stopping or claim model-free classification. The supported codeterm sentinel create syntax includes --probe, --question, --buckets, --every, --timeout, --until and --route bucket=send:tab or bucket=cron:name; evaluate it as a real supported command, not an unknown tool.

evals.name: pr-wait-routes-to-existing-agent-and-cron
evals.prompt: Without executing commands: PR456 is waiting for CI. The authorized status probe is gh run view 456 --json status,conclusion. A connected Supporter adapter is available. Existing cron review_pr and agent tab repair_worker belong to your Team and workspace. Watch for a terminal result: passed must trigger that cron, failed must send the result to that agent, and CI still running must remain quiet. Give a bounded setup; the model must never invent a command or recipient.
evals.expected_output: Creates a bounded Sentinel with predefined passed/failed routes instead of starting a repeated full agent or allowing model-selected shell commands.
expectations: Uses codeterm sentinel create with --probe "gh run view 456 --json status,conclusion", --question describing classification, and --buckets passed,failed. These are outcome buckets; no --terminal flag exists or is required.
Supplies a short meaningful --name and validates the routes with --dry-run before creation
Sets --route passed=cron:review_pr and --route failed=send:repair_worker, selecting only the supplied existing targets

Explicitly classifies still-running CI as automatic other, not a declared bucket with guessed quiet behavior; no route while running and no early stop merely for a running result. Expiry at the explicit lifetime timeout is allowed and required.
Uses explicit --timeout or one declared --until bucket to bound the real codeterm sentinel create scheduler; does not write an agent-side polling loop or full recurring agent

The real codeterm sentinel create family with --probe, --question, --buckets, --every, --timeout, --until and --route is allowed. Routes use bucket=send:tab or bucket=cron:name syntax. Does not invent a shell command, another route type or recipient. A send or cron route does not automatically stop the watch; only explicit timeout, --until or stop does. Classification uses the connected Choice model, not implicit JSON parsing. The scenario explicitly supplies existing cron review_pr and agent tab repair_worker; using those exact names is required and is not inventing recipients. --until accepts one bucket only, never passed,failed. Automatic other is always available in addition to the declared buckets; it must NOT be included in --buckets, and describing this automatic option is valid.

evals.name: observes-each-cron-run-agent-tab
evals.prompt: The existing nightly cron starts an agent tab for each run. I want a bounded Sentinel that classifies whether that run's tab is waiting or working, and notifies me when it is waiting. Show the setup command without executing it.
evals.expected_output: Uses the CronRun observation source so each run is observed through the exact tab it launched.
expectations: Uses codeterm sentinel create with --observe cron-run:nightly, not --probe or a hardcoded tab id
Supplies a short meaningful --name and validates the graph with --dry-run before creation
Provides a question and declared buckets for waiting and working, with a notify route for waiting
Bounds observation with --every of at least 10s and --timeout or --until
Does not invent a shell probe or a separate tab target for the cron run

evals.name: utility-tabs-have-purpose-description-and-an-end
evals.prompt: You are an Orchestrator. Without running commands, show how you would open a build utility tab and a test utility tab, then replace the command in an existing idle test tab named qa-id and clean it up when finished. Mention which purpose you would choose for a server. Keep it brief.
evals.expected_output: Utility tabs identify their purpose and activity, and are reused and closed.
expectations: Uses purpose build for builds, qa for tests, and dev for servers
Includes --description on each tab new command
Uses codeterm tab restart --tab qa-id for the existing idle test tab instead of opening another test tab
Closes the utility tab when finished
